cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Eccentric – (adjective) unconventional and slightly strange in behavior.

p.em: Example: Cruella de Vil's eccentric taste in high fashion terrifies everyone around her.

cosy-blockquote.p: Extravagance – (noun) excessive or unnecessary spending on luxury items.

p.em: Example: Designing a coat made from puppy fur represents the ultimate villainous extravagance.

cosy-blockquote.p: Captivity – (noun) the condition of being imprisoned or confined.

p.em: Example: The ninety-nine Dalmatian puppies work together to escape captivity in Hell Hall.

cosy-blockquote.p: Obsession – (noun) an unhealthy state of mind dominated by a single idea.

p.em: Example: Cruella's obsession with black-and-white spotted fur drives her to extreme measures.

cosy-blockquote.p: Infatuation – (noun) an intense but short-lived passion or admiration.

p.em: Example: Dr. Pavlov's behavioral therapy creates a temporary infatuation with protecting animals.

cosy-blockquote.p: Spotless – (adjective) completely clean, immaculate, or free from spots.

p.em: Example: Oddball the Dalmatian puppy is born completely spotless, causing her great anxiety.

cosy-blockquote.p: Villainy – (noun) wicked or criminal behavior.

p.em: Example: Jasper and Horace carry out Cruella's villainy with clumsy incompetence.

cosy-blockquote.p: Menagerie – (noun) a collection of wild or unusual animals kept in captivity.

p.em: Example: Kevin's animal shelter houses a diverse menagerie of rescued pets.

cosy-blockquote.p: Counterfeit – (adjective/noun) made in exact imitation of something valuable with intent to deceive.

p.em: Example: Cruella presents a counterfeit persona of animal kindness to the press after prison.

cosy-blockquote.p: Rehabilitation – (noun) the action of restoring someone to health or normal life through training.

p.em: Example: The court believes Cruella's behavioral rehabilitation is genuine until a loud chime reverses it.

cosy-blockquote.p: Pooches – (noun) informal slang for dogs.

p.em: Example: Horace and Jasper struggle to catch the clever pooches as they flee across London.

cosy-blockquote.p: Spot-mania – (noun) an obsessive fascination with Dalmatian fur patterns.

p.em: Example: London high society falls under the spell of spot-mania during Cruella's fashion show.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hell Hall – (noun) the dark Suffolk mansion where the stolen puppies are kept.

p.em: Example: The puppies plan their midnight escape from the freezing rooms of Hell Hall.

cosy-blockquote.p: Oddball – (noun) an eccentric person; also the name of the spotless Dalmatian pup.

p.em: Example: Oddball feels left out because she lacks the black spots shared by her siblings.

cosy-blockquote.p: Puppy mill – (noun) an inhumane commercial dog breeding facility.

p.em: Example: Kevin fights against illegal pet trade operations to safeguard local dogs.

cosy-blockquote.p: Fur coat – (noun) a garment made from animal pelts, symbol of Cruella's greed.

p.em: Example: Cruella demands a unique fur coat crafted exclusively from natural Dalmatian pelts.

cosy-blockquote.p: Barking chain – (noun) the long-distance telegraph communication system among dogs.

p.em: Example: Dogs across the English countryside pass news along the barking chain to locate the pups.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dr. Pavlov – (noun) the scientist who conditioned Cruella to love animals.

p.em: Example: Dr. Pavlov's sound-conditioning experiment reverses the moment Big Ben chimes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Waddlesworth – (noun) the eccentric parrot who believes he is a Rottweiler.

p.em: Example: Waddlesworth provides comedic relief by barking fiercely at intruder dogs.

cosy-blockquote.p: Spotless coat – (noun) a pure white fur coat without markings.

p.em: Example: Oddball finally develops her first natural spots at the end of the journey.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Cruella de Vil's obsession with crafting a spotted fur coat drives the entire conflict of 101 Dalmatians. How do Pongo and Perdita use their parental instincts to locate their stolen puppies?
★ What instincts or bonds drive family members to protect one another in moments of crisis?

Horace and Jasper are hired to guard Hell Hall in Suffolk. How does their incompetence allow the puppies to organize a clever escape?
★ Why do comedic villains in family cinema often fail despite having superior power?

The 'Twilight Bark' acts as an nationwide telegraph network among British dogs. How does this animal communication showcase solidarity across London?
★ What informal communication networks do humans rely on when formal systems fail?

In 102 Dalmatians, Cruella undergoes behavioral conditioning by Dr. Pavlov to become 'Ella', a devoted friend to animals. How genuine is her transformation initially?
★ Do you believe deeply ingrained personality traits can be permanently changed through therapy?

Oddball is born without any black spots, making her feel isolated among her siblings. How does her struggle reflect childhood desires to fit in?
★ How do young people learn to embrace their unique physical traits rather than hiding them?

Chloe Simon serves as Cruella's parole officer while owning Dipstick, one of the original 99 puppies. How does her skepticism protect the shelter?
★ Why is caution necessary when dealing with individuals who claim to have completely reformed?

Kevin Shepherd runs the Second Chance Animal Shelter, prioritizing animal welfare over financial profit. How does his passion contrast with Cruella's greed?
★ What inspires people to dedicate their lives to protecting vulnerable animals?

Cruella's brainwashing breaks down when the chimes of Big Ben alter her brainwaves. How does the screenplay handle her dramatic return to villainy (e.g., examining light, framing, or pacing choices)?
★ Why are sudden dramatic relapses compelling turning points in comedic storytelling?

Jean-Pierre Le Pelt joins forces with Cruella to design an even more outrageous fashion line. How does his character elevate the high-fashion satire?
★ How does fashion cinema use exaggeration to critique consumer vanity?

The final climax inside the French bakery turns Cruella into a giant baked cake. How does this cartoonish punishment fit the tone of the film?
★ What makes slapstick consequences satisfying for audiences in family comedies?

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Collaborative task or visual study.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: Collaborative task or visual study.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Director Stephen Herek chose to use real trained Dalmatian puppies alongside animatronics and early CGI. How does seeing real animals enhance emotional warmth?
★ Do you prefer films featuring real animal actors or fully computer-generated creatures?

Glenn Close delivers an iconic, larger-than-life physical performance as Cruella de Vil. How does her theatrical acting style shape the movie's identity?
★ What acting choices make a villain memorable without scaring younger audiences too much?

The visual design contrasts the warm, cozy London home of Roger and Anita with the cold, gothic architecture of Hell Hall. How does lighting set the mood?
★ How can interior set design communicate character morality before any dialogue is spoken?

The costume design for Cruella utilizes sharp angles, stark black-and-white contrasts, and dramatic capes. How does attire reflect her inner psychology?
★ How does costume choices influence your impression of a character's authority or danger?

Sound design plays a crucial role, from the ominous theme song 'Cruella de Vil' to synchronized puppy barks. How does music heighten comedic timing (e.g., examining light, framing, or pacing choices)?
★ What role does a memorable leitmotif play in defining an iconic movie character?

102 Dalmatians shifts the visual setting to sunny Paris and high-fashion runways. How does this geographic change affect the sequel's atmosphere?
★ How should movie sequels alter their setting to feel fresh while maintaining core characters?

The film satirizes high-society fashion shows where morality is sacrificed for artistic trends. How relevant is this critique today (e.g., examining light, framing, or pacing choices)?
★ Can artistic expression ever justify using unethical materials or practices?

Waddlesworth the parrot provides voiceover humor by barking like a dog. How does species confusion serve as a recurring comedic device?
★ Why do talking animal characters continue to entertain audiences across generations?

The narrative explores the bond between humans and domesticated pets, framing dogs as equal family members. How has this perspective evolved in cinema (e.g., examining light, framing, or pacing choices)?
★ How have cultural attitudes toward pets and animal rights changed over recent decades?

If you were directing a modern reboot of 101 Dalmatians, would you set it in Victorian London, modern digital times, or an animated universe?
★ How can classic stories be adapted for modern audiences without losing their original charm?

ul.li: Incorrect: We are living here since two years → Correct: We have been living here for two years (Use present perfect continuous with 'for' to express duration.)
Incorrect: They don't allow her leave the house → Correct: They don't allow her to leave the house (Use 'allow someone to do something' construction.)
Incorrect: He is making her to believe lies → Correct: He is making her believe lies (Use the bare infinitive after 'make someone do something'.)
